You know it's been raining non-stop today. The garden is underwater and I'm worried about how it's affecting our health, both mental and physical. Yes, the weather's been relentless, hasn't it? It's not just the physical issues like the garden or possible flood warnings. This constant rain can have quite a negative impact on our moods too. You two never had to deal with this when you were lecturing up in London, did you? Oh, we had our rainy days for sure! But there's always a silver lining, isn't there? I used to find that the rain actually helped students stay focused and made for a cozy, study atmosphere. True, but living through persistent rain can get old quickly. It's not just about the weather, though. We've been talking about our health, and how it's impacting our daily lives. Have you both considered investing in some decent umbrellas or rain gear? You know, to make it easier when you need to go out. I think we need something a bit more radical than umbrellas. This rain is relentless! But on a serious note, have you seen the technology out there? I've been looking into some new boots that are waterproof, breathable, and have a built in heater. For really cold wet days, they could be a game changer! I saw those on a tech show last week. They're quite something. I think that could be a good investment for our trips to town or on the days when one just has to face the rain. Oh, I've always been fascinated by wearable tech. Especially since my days at the university when we discussed the future of healthcare and how wearables could monitor our health and report any issues back to us or to our doctors. That sounds like a more appealing thought than the rain. Let's look into it. If it's good for our health, and makes daily life easier, it might be worth the investment. Alright then, sounds like a plan. Let's look at those boots and maybe some other tech to make rainy days a bit more bearable. And speaking of tech, has anyone seen the new consoles coming out? Oh, I've been eyeing the PlayStation 5. They say it's a significant improvement over the previous models. I'm more into PC gaming myself, but I've heard the PS5 is quite something too.

So, I hear that Cassie's wedding is coming up soon, right? Yeah, it's going to be such an exciting day! I talked to her recently and she was beaming about the venue and the decorations. She and Max are both so chill about the whole process. I'm kind of jealous of how relaxed they are about it all. I know, right? Marriage seems so big and scary sometimes, but actually, seeing our friends doing it makes it feel more like it’s just a natural step in life. Totally. Cassie said she's most excited about the wedding party. She's been planning it with our other friends from uni. I’m sure it’ll be amazing. And I hear there'll be a big dinner the night before? Ah, Cassie mentioned that. She’s invitation-only, but she’s trying to include as many of us as possible, I hope. Yeah, she said she’s thinking of a smaller, more intimate group for the dinner so people can get to know each other. But for the actual wedding, it’s gonna be a much bigger gang. That sounds perfect. We should make sure to ask her about the boys’ outfit for the dinner. You know, to coordinate or something. Ooh good idea! We should send a group message to the girls and boys and suggest matching something. Maybe bow ties or something fun? Like matching socks? That could be cute. And in all seriousness, maybe we can also start planning a babysitter for the evening. Some of us will probably need it. Or we could just leave the kids with the parents that day. Problem solved! True. And what if one of us volunteers to take a group photo or two of all of us together during the celebration? Would be nice for the memory book. Great idea! I think either me or Alex can handle that. Alex is always good with a camera. Definitely. Let’s all plan to be there, cheer on Cassie and Max, and make sure we have our biggest smiles on and a bottle of something bubbly. And hopefully, zero awkward dance moments. Ha! That's the goal. And once this is over, maybe we can plan a post-wedding girls’ dinner. Celebrate ourself and catch up. I’d love that! Let’s raise a glass to Cassie and Max and all that matrimonial stuff.

I talked to old Bobby the other day down by the butcher’s shop. You know him, don't you? He says his grandson's got one o' them fancy new phones that can do all sorts of tricks. I couldn’t believe it. Say, can it really take pictures with that ghostly depth and make you look like you’re floating? I thought he was spinning me a yarn for my old ears. Oh, yes, it can. You'll need one to see, really. It's not just pictures – it can even pay for things, like your shopping, or even do your banking. Sent your grandkids down to show you? No, haven’t gotten around to it yet. They’re all so busy with their own lives. You know how it is when the young ones get into these new gadgets. They spend more time liking each other’s faces than talking to each other. [chuckles] It's true. But for all the talk about it making us antisocial, it's also brought us closer in this house. One moment we’re all on our own devices, the next we’re swapping silly videos. Reminds me of when the VCR came out. We thought that was peak technology at the time. [chuckles] I remember. We had to get one for the house because the kids were always at my place watching videos. Now, it's all streaming and cloud-based and whatnot. I get that it's useful, but sometimes I feel like they're losing the ability to just sit and play like we did with real toys. I think there's room for both, really. My grandkids still love riding their bikes or playing in the garden, but they also love their tablets for learning and games. Balancing it all, I reckon, is the key. If only money were as easy to balance! [laughs] We've been having a bit of a tough month with some unexpected bills. It's reminded me that making ends meet is still a challenge, no matter your age. [nodding] I often think about just how different it is from when I grew up. Couldn’t afford a bike till I had a paper round. Now the little ones are lucky if they even have to mow the lawn once in a while. You're right. I used to horse ride, and that came with a hefty cost too.

Ah, thank you so much for inviting me over, it’s lovely catching up with you. How’s the family been?      They’re doing well, thanks. The grandkids continue to be a handful but that keeps me on my toes.      I can imagine. I’m sure you’re getting your fill of that with trying to teach English to students.      Well, it’s a job that never gets old. Every day brings new challenges. What about you though? How's the language teaching going?      It’s rewarding. I’m actually quite interested in the similarities and differences between languages these days. For instance, German and English have far more in common than one might think.      Fascinating. I used to have quite a bit of German at school but never got around to mastering it. You’re kind of inspiring me to pick up where I left off.      You totally should, there are some wonderful resources now, especially online courses. And did you hear about that new studies suggesting language learning might even help with cognitive aging?      I did hear something about that. One never stops learning, right? I’m also thinking of getting back into that model train hobby I had years ago. Or maybe something else entirely. What about your weekends?      Oh, weekends are usually all about language or just planning lessons. But when I can, I love getting outdoors - hiking, that kind of thing, if the weather’s decent.      Same here. Though I’ve had to adjust my expectations since retiring. Last weekend I was helping out at the local heritage club changing the exhibit. It reminded me of my time managing a business, but in a far more relaxed setting.      That’s great, keeping active, keeping engaged, it’s so important. Reminds me, we should have a family lunch soon.      Yes, could do. And maybe we can even plan a weekend somewhere in the countryside. We could all do with a bit of a break.      Sounds like a plan. And between you and me, maybe I’ll finally persuade you to learn those essential German phrases I’ve been suggesting.      You... I'll think about it. But be gentle, okay?      I'll bring along that old textbook of yours too, make it less intimidating.      Ah youth! Always so enthusiastic, always so cheeky.      That’s living!      Indeed it is. Now, shall we get back to that tea? It’s going cold, and I reckon we’ve got another hour of conversation in us before needing another brew.

So Grace, today's Valentine's Day. How's yours going? You know, just another day of studying. I didn’t bother with anything fancy though, the only heart I need pounding is for my questions on this exam next week. But how about you, have you got any plans or did you even get out of your room today? Oh, for me it was even worse. I wanted to watch a movie with my flatmates, something silly and comforting, but one of them had to deal with a family emergency, and the other had a sudden stomach bug. So it was just me with my laptop and a pizza, feeling like I was the only one in London not in a relationship. That’s rough. But look at the bright side, you get to do all Valentine's fun on your terms now. What did you end up watching? I settled on something funny. Watched "Crazy Rich Asians" again because I hadn’t seen it in ages. It always puts me in a good mood, plus I've been meaning to learn more about Asian cinema because I'm studying film studies. That’s cool! I love that movie. The food scenes make me crave really nice food. Speaking of, have you tried out that new Thai place near the university? I went there with some course friends last week, it was amazing. No, I haven’t, actually. I swear all my downtime is spent working or stuck in my head with my dissertation topics… But that sounds great. Maybe we can try it out next week? Just the two of us, no commitments. Sounds like a plan. And who knows, maybe we'll make it a tradition. I feel like the idea of a Valentine's Day without a partner is overhyped. Like, why can't we just enjoy ourselves anyway, right? There’s always someone to celebrate with, even if it’s just each other. Like two lonely souls finding comfort in a plate of pad thai. I love that take. And let’s be honest, the food is always better when it’s not an obligation. But have you noticed how even the biggest anti-Valentine's Day people post something sentimental just for the day? It’s all so performative. Yeah. I saw something on Instagram thinking, "Really? You just made all these progress updates and suddenly now you're reduced to a single post about loving someone?"...

So have you seen Grace's latest article; it's really well done. Yeah, I talked to her about the research for that piece. It's heartbreaking to see how deep-rooted the housing issue is, especially in Kensal Rise – do you have any plans to tackle this in your work? Actually, one of my projects is looking into affordable housing solutions and how they can actually be integrated into new developments. The owners are often very set against it, but even if it's just a few units, it makes a difference. Yeah, but the problem is, there's always profit to be made with expensive developments and I don't see that changing in London. Capitalism just says go for the most profitable. Exactly! And racism plays a big part in making sure certain communities get overlooked. Hence why predominantly BME areas seem to get forgotten about when it comes to regeneration or investment. It's like they think the only way forward is gentrification, which means pushing out the very people who have lived there for generations. Absolutely. But that doesn’t mean we don’t keep pushing back. I've been reading up on anti-racist urban planning, which introduces a kind of anti-oppression framework – it's about seeing the landscape and development as a tool for social justice rather than just profit or aesthetics. Well, at least you're addressing it in your work. Honestly though, I feel like it's an uphill battle in journalism too, because if you keep pointing out racial disparities, some people accuse you of being biased and "political." Unfortunately, that's part of the backlash. It's why I try to contextualise and provide clear data and policy examples, so it's not perceived as just opinion. Yeah, same thing. I tried to get a piece published about how certain communities were affected more by the pandemic, citing concrete data and research by epidemiologists, but they wouldn't publish it. Because they're changing the narrative to not address the disproportionate impact on BME communities… Exactly. I don't know, it’s like they just hope it all just fades away so we stop talking about it. And it's not just media; it's everywhere – education, the job market. That's why we need to keep talking about it and maybe someday they'll have to listen. Yeah, plus now with these new segregation reports coming out.

Oh, talked to [Name of nursery] today. You're actually starting next week! Oh, yes, I remember hearing that! That’ll be quite the change for [Baby’s Name], won't it? Absolutely! It's big for both of you, actually. Now that you’re getting back to uni too, how do you feel about that? Honestly, I'm a bit nervous. It feels like ages since I was in proper classes – and with a baby at home, I’ll have to manage time wisely. I know what you mean. When I was in work, the juggling act was intense. But you'll get into a rhythm. And you know you can always ask for help when you need it, either from your university or here at home? Thanks, Mum. That does help. I've actually been thinking about potential future holidays. Maybe when [Baby's Name] is a bit older or even just short breaks. Oh, that sounds fun! When [Baby's Name] is weaned, it'll be easier for short trips. And while the baby's still small, maybe the grandparents could help at home? Yeah, that's a plan. Grandma and Grandpa keep offering to help out, so that’d be perfect for short breaks. Good idea. And we should definitely plan for a proper family holiday too once the baby’s a bit older and more settled. Mum, doesn’t TV seem so slow when you watch it with the baby now? Everything else feels so fast-paced. Oh, totally! But there are some gems, you know. Have you caught the new BBC documentary series? It’s really good fun for grown-ups too. Actually, I did see that one! Quite enjoyed it. But you’re right, when it's changing the baby’s nappies and making meals, everything else does seem slower by comparison. Well, that's just new parenthood. But it’s worth it! And take advantage of TV for your downtime—it’s not all rubbish. I know, sometimes those kids’ shows are almost as entertaining as the grown-up ones . I’ll say! They're definitely teaching me patience. I can imagine. You know, this transition to nursery and you going back to uni is...we’re all adjusting. But we’ll get through it together. And if anyone can handle it, it's definitely us. Thanks, Mum. That means a lot. Just trying to be helpful, love.

So, how was everyone's day?      It was just the usual. Collected a fair few hundred pounds for the charity today. Going to present the cheque next week, and I'm sure we've passed the target comfortably now.      Congratulations! That’s impressive. How did the fundraiser go?      It was at a coffee morning at the community center. Lots of local businesses came forward and donated generously.      I’ve been reviewing the sales reports for today. Might have to cut a bit back on expenses next month. The EE phone bill looks particularly steep.      What happened? Did you go over your limit or is it a one-off?      Just a lot of conference calls and video meetings. But I think it might have been a mistake on their side. I’m going to call them and confirm.      Did any new charity projects come up today?      Not really, mostly just busy with the current fundraiser. But we’ve had an interest in expanding services. Might need to think about that over the next few months.      I’ve got a meeting with the store's regional supplier on Tuesday to discuss some new product placements. Hoping we can get some more premium items in stock.      Speaking of which, I need to arrange a trial with the new software provider. First week of next month. Want to make sure it integrates with our existing system properly.      Don’t forget we’ve got the family trip planned for the weekend after next. Right?      Yes, just me, you, the kids, and the grandkids are going to the national reserve. Hopefully, the weather will play along.      Make sure to book the picnic permits and changing facilities.      And can we also check if there's a charity event there we can pop into or support?      Good idea. I’ll look into it.      Also, got a funny story for you all. Today at the store, someone tried to pay with an expired card...      Oh yeah?      The customer was mortified when we told them it wasn’t working. But he then pulled out another one just to prove it wasn’t a mistake on his end.      haha, classic.      That’s a good one.      Seems like everyone's day has its own share of challenges and triumphs.      I'd say so.      Definitely.         So, about that EE bill—have you spoken to them yet?      Just about to, actually. Might have a quick word with them during dinner.

Great to see you mate. How's the garden business been doing? Well it's been alright. Had a few tough jobs down by the river. Had to fight off some pond algae. Still it's honest work and it's a joy to see something grow from seed. That's nice. Speaking of growth, have you been into anything new on TV? Any shows caught your eye? To be honest, I've been watching a bit of Roman history documentaries. You know, alongside all the medieval stuff. Really interesting seeing how those ancient civilizations operated. Fascinating, isn't it? I've been watching this show called "Spartacus". It's pretty graphic but it's incredible to see how short their lives were compared to ours. Yeah, and to think about all the early deaths from plagues and diseases they didn't even understand back then... While we're on the topic of history, did you ever think about how different musicians would've reacted to modern day conditions? That's an interesting thought! We could have a Chopin and Beethoven comparison. Chopin died at 39 mostly due to the conditions and stress. Where as Beethoven lived till 56 despite his deafness. It's amazing he composed such beautiful music even when he couldn't hear anything. Well, technology has certainly come a long way. Speaking of modern conveniences, have you tried this tea from the new shop down in town? They really know how to balance flavors. I have. It’s pretty good! But I've also been buying a lot of spices lately. I've been experimenting with some old recipes from my grandmother. She always used to say that a good mortar and pestle is essential for the right flavor. Yeah, I've also been exploring more with spices. I've been making my own spice mixes. Just got this new thing with cumin, coriander, and garlic and it's been amazing with roasted chickpeas. That’s a good one. I've tried chickpeas but never thought to add cumin. It’s like adding a whole new layer of flavor isn't it? And speaking of new flavors, have you tried seitan? It's like a meat substitute but made from wheat gluten. Yeah, I've heard of it. Haven't tried it myself though. Yeah, it's quite good. Could be a good change if you're looking to reduce meat or just want something different.

So have you got the French dictée done yet? Not yet, I'm doing it right now. Is it hard? It's a bit tricky, but I think I kind of understand it. We had a good lesson last week. Lucky! I wish I had a class with Monsieur Dupont again. Yeah, he was so fun even though it is French. Anyway, how was your art lesson? I heard you were supposed to paint something abstract? Oh, it was alright but I wasn’t really sure what to do. Mrs. Jenkins says it’s about expressing ourselves, but I ended up just drawing a nice tree again. LOL, that doesn’t sound like expressing much! I tried to do something with shapes and colours but it ended up looking like a soup. Exactly! Next time, I’m just going to paint whatever comes to mind and say it’s abstract. For sure! We should have a study group for this test though. Maybe we can swap notes or anything? That would be great! What time can we meet? How about tomorrow before school? We can grab breakfast together and go over the key points for the test. Yeah, that sounds great! And after school, can we practice the wind band for the concert? Of course! It’s only a few more weeks until the concert doesn’t it? Yeah, that’s kind of scary. I hope we nailed our parts, especially if one of us has to solo. Same here! But I’m sure we’ll do great. We’ve practiced a lot since the summer ended. It’s just that Mr. Smith really emphasizes clarity and expression in our English lessons, and changing the tone and mood really threw me off on the test. I know what you mean! For the next test, maybe I can make some flashcards for tone words and stuff. That would be awesome! You’re really good at making those. Thanks! So, this Saturday, we’re all going to meet at ANON’s place to study and practice, right? Yep, I saw the message. It’s from 9 to 12. Don’t forget your instruments and whatever you need for the English test. Right, don’t forget! We’re also talking about maybe planning a trip together for the summer if we can somehow save up. How about that? What do you want to do?

So, Peter and I were talking last week and he mentioned about getting his car serviced. Have you heard anything about this new mechanic in town? I hope I can trust him with my old set of wheels.      Haven't heard anything specific about him but I've noticed more people around here buying electric cars. Thought about it for my truck, but I'm more worried about the cost. What’s your take on it, is it worth the initial investment?      Prices are coming down quickly, and it’s definitely a future-proof choice. Plus, the reduction in maintenance costs and being more environmentally friendly...      Well, when it comes to electric, you’re always on about this and that. But for us, it’s more about what we can afford. Our budget is tightly tied to this house, let alone cars.      But with electric vehicles coming more mainstream, it’s only a matter of time before it becomes the norm. The gov’t is even offering incentives to make it more accessible. Though, it still comes down to personal choice and priorities.   Speaker_1 :   Speaking of incentives, isn’t it remarkable how the current health crisis has also drawn attention to the benefits of a healthier lifestyle? Exercise and diet are no longer just health topics but economic and social ones too.      Certainly. Just last weekend, I helped my neighbor start riding his bike again. He said he’s determined to lose some weight and get healthier. It’s inspiring to see people taking their health into their own hands.      Obesity, diet, exercise—it’s all linked to our genes, but also to lifestyle choices. I remember when Jane was younger, our doctor would always say, "It runs in the family." I thought it was destined, but now people say it’s not so much about destiny but what you do with the genes you’ve got.      Exactly. Our understanding of genetics has grown so much. It’s about managing the genetic risk rather than being enslaved to it. Whether it’s health or potential for disease, we have more control than we knew.      In thinking about control, I wonder how much of it is tied to what we believe in. I know some people find comfort and motivation through their religious beliefs.      Certainly, it helps provide a framework for many. Me though, I always said I’d deal with what life throws at me; no scripture needed.

So have you managed to figure out how to set up the assignments and quizzes on Moodle yet? Well, I've tried to follow the guide, but I've just hit a roadblock. I can’t seem to find how to properly link assignments to the gradebook or set them up for peer review. Oh, I've been there! But actually, I've been there a few times. All right, let me walk you through how I've set mine up this semester. That’d be great. I've been lazy setting assignments manually for too long, relying on email and file sharing more than intended. Haha, same. But trust me, once you’ve got it set up, it’s a huge time saver, and organization-wise, it’s much better. Plus, students seem to appreciate the clear pathway and feedback process. Exactly, the feedback part excites me. But honestly, I couldn’t figure out how to make it all sequential. I wanted the assignment or quiz to depend on the completion of the previous one. But basically, in the settings of a module or a week , you have to carefully set conditions for availability. This includes whether students need to complete A before B. Conditions for availability, right? I remember seeing that term around, but I couldn’t click my way to it. Let me grab my laptop and walk you through the steps from the start. [Opens laptop] Perfect, thanks! I just need to see the pathway.   [Please note: An actual technical walk-through and real Moodle setup details are not included here as it requires a visual setup guide, which this format can’t accommodate fully but would be explained in great detail in an actual conversation.]   Right, so first, go to your course and click on the week or module where you want the assignment or quiz to be. Then, on the left, click on 'Turn editing on' so you can make changes. Now, if you're setting up a new assignment or quiz, click on the 'Add an activity or resource' button and select what you need. Okay, add activity or resource I got. What about linking it to the gradebook or setting it for peer review? Ah, excellent questions. For the gradebook, when you're setting up the assignment or quiz, down at the bottom of the settings page, there’s an option to 'Edit settings' on the right of 'Grade type' - usually, it’s set to 'no' grading by default.

I'm really sensitive to jetlag. It's been quite challenging to adjust. Still feel like I'm floating after three hours of sleep last night. I know what you mean. But think about it, this is minor compared to the sleep deprivation that's coming our way with the new baby. Now that's serious jetlag! True, very true. Although at least this time I can get some caffeine to help, and I'm not responsible for anything else’s well-being at the moment. Exactly. And just like jetlag, you'll get used to the new routine in time but for now, every night feels like we're on a different time zone. It's amazing how quickly the body can adjust to these extreme situations. But speaking of babies... how’s the nursery coming along? Did you finish setting up the crib and changing station? Just finished those up last weekend. I took advantage of the quiet evenings to get it all ready. It feels good to have it done, but at the same time, it's a weird mix of emotions—excitement and maybe a hint of fear about what’s coming. Fear is natural, but we've been through all the classes and reading. We're as prepared as we can be, right? I mean, there’s still so much we can't plan for, but I feel more confident now. Definitely. And we've got a great support system. Plus, doesn’t it feel like every single couple we know is either expecting now or has babes around the same age? It makes it all seem less daunting in a way. It definitely helps to know we’re not alone in this. Speaking of connections, have we finalized who we’re taking to the local dramatic performance next week? We talked about maybe taking the in-laws if they’re up for it. Let’s send a group message to all and see who’s interested. I also want to check for handicap accessible seating and if we need to book in advance because I heard it’s quite popular. Great idea. And let's also make sure we have a good cushion for the baby’s schedule in case he decides to keep us up the night before. Always better to be prepared. Speaking of schedules, how’s our current routine going with baby?

So tell me about your friend over in Kurdistan who was having trouble getting his visa. Oh, that would be my brother-in-law. He's talked about it a lot, and well, let's just say that getting visas in his time wasn't that easy, nor was it consistent with fair practice. It questions the status of his identity and his rights as a Kurdish individual, you know? He's part of a community that has been continually subjected to bureaucratic hurdles as if their nationality isn't fully recognized. That's interesting. You know, alongside this, I've been following the oil politics in the Middle East, especially with the recent dealings in Libya. It's such a dynamic, isn't it? Absolutely, and oil is a bit like a double-edged sword for us in the region. On one hand, it's a significant source of income. On the other, it's led to so much exploitation and corrupt governance. And let's not forget the Wahhabi influence, which often seems to have ulterior motives when it comes to engaging with these oil-rich regions. It's got a major impact on the youth, really. Many young people feel like there are no progressive outlets for this wealth, just more conflict and religious extremism being pushed. I see. It's kind of assumed in the West that it's about mere religious zeal, but as you're saying, it's also about power, control, and money. Ah, and to make matters worse, many of these regions, especially where oil is found, have been experiencing a serious brain drain. Talented young people are either forced to leave or they're encouraged to "help" in ways that don't align with their values. Makes the visa issues your brother-in-law faced even more serious, doesn't it? It's one more obstacle for people who want to contribute positively to the region's future. Exactly. The international community needs to consider that our friends and family over there are not just individuals trying to migrate but people who want to confront these issues and rebuild, but they need the breathing room - the passport, the visa - to do so. Absolutely. On a different note, I'm actually moving house soon. Fun but exhausting. Congratulations, by the way! That's a big life change. But fracturing out of all her healthy habits like that. It's like... how is it that easy? I think it's about the peer pressure. Like when you're new to a place, you just want to fit in, you know? Might just be down to the fact uni can be overwhelming. You're in a new city, new environment, new people. Smoking's just... an easy way out. But I thought she was into this whole feminist thing? How does that reconcile with smoking, which is barely feminist considering the tobacco industry doesn't exactly have great track records on gender equality or health in general. That's a really good point actually. I don't know maybe it's just about how people balance their beliefs with personal habits or coping mechanisms. Yeah, maybe. But it's genuinely concerning. I'm all for people having things to themselves but you can't ignore the health impacts. It's also about privilege, perhaps. I mean, being able to choose not to smoke can sometimes be a privilege linked to your socio-economic status, access to information and all that. Exactly. Plus doesn't it kind of undermine the feminist cause if we can't even control our own addiction or poor health habits? True. And let's not forget about the side of commerce; they market these products so strategically, making it seem like it’s a choice rather than a trap. Oh totally. It’s just so manipulative. And what's with the aesthetic of smoking being cool or rebellious? It's so outdated. It's all about cultural perceptions. I mean, some people genuinely don't know any better or haven't had the education about it, or they just want to feel older or sophisticated for a bit. So, the question is, how do we even have this conversation with people in a way that isn't just lecturing or judging? I think if you're close, you just gently bring it up.

Speaker_1 :   You know, Emma, I've been thinking about this friend of mine from drama school – Rachel. We were really close back then but since we left and started different paths, it just feels...off?   Speaker_2 :   Oh, I've had that too. Like, someone from uni or work who was super close and now feels like a whole different person in your life.      Exactly! Like, every time we try to meet up it's just this awkward tension. I try to talk to her like we used to but she's...changed. Her whole life, attitude, everything. It's like trying to talk to someone new.      I feel that sometimes too. You know, with people you used to be close to but then they got into this job or these new hobbies or friends and it feels like you're on entirely different wavelengths.      But the problem is, this is a person I don't really want to see anymore but feel weird about cutting ties with. We've got this shared history, but the connection feels dead. How do you phase out someone like that?      It's tough. For me, it was about realizing it's okay to prioritize current relationships or friendships that actually feel nourishing. There's this guilt sometimes in suggesting we don’t hang out as much or in general making less effort. But if it’s not working, you need to acknowledge that.      I know, but the how-to is tricky. Just dropping off the face of the earth feels harsh, and I don’t want things to get weird.      I just tried being less reactive to messages or invitations. If I don't respond for a while or suggest we catch up less frequently, it's less confrontational but still gets the message across.      Yes, that’s a smart approach. Gradually letting things fade – it’s kinder for both parties in a way. But what if they just keep trying to hang out because they want to relive the past or because they're unaware of the change?      That’s where you need to communicate, even if just indirectly. If they repeatedly ask to meet up but you don’t feel like it, you can say something like, "I've got a pretty packed schedule right now and I want to focus on this new [hobby/interest/project]." You're not shutting them down completely but setting boundaries.

Speaker_1 :   You know I've just seen this thing on Facebook about people with OCD and how some kind of new treatment isn't working for them.   Speaker_2 :   I had a few kids with very light cases of chicken pox at my place once. Nothing too serious but it was a bit of a worry to some of the parents.   Speaker_3 :   Yeah I've read that too, it's actually quite interesting what they're trying to do in terms of behavioral therapy now.   Speaker_4 :   Exactly, and it's also important to address the stigma around mental health conditions like OCD. Some people might think that it's just people being particular about tidiness, but it’s much deeper than that.      For me, it's always about understanding and respecting people's experiences. Not everyone who is tidy or diligent has OCD, you know. It's about the severity of it affecting their daily life.      I used to tell my charges that it's normal to feel a certain level of anxiety, but for some, it's taken over. Speaking of things being taken over... does anyone else sometimes find themselves doing little things because they’re used to, and they might not even realize it?      That doesn’t necessarily suggest OCD but sometimes we just develop habits without even realizing. The issue becomes when those habits interfere with our ability to function normally or make us unhappy.      I’ve had students who weren’t diagnosed, but they showed some traits. It can be tough to navigate, especially when you’re younger and trying to figure out who you are.      While I was younger, the word "religious" could trigger some confusion. I mean, I was brought up to go to church every Sunday, but in these new times, I see a lot of people expressing belief in a more personal way. Makes me wonder if we’ve moved away from organized religion or are finding other ways to connect spiritually.      I think it’s just the ways people experience faith changing. Some find more peace in meditation or personal reflection than traditional church services. It still leads back to wanting to make sense of things, thinking there’s something bigger than just us.      Sure, but often these deeper beliefs or practices that replace organized religion can also feel very ritualistic or compulsive. It’s a thin line, yeah?      Exactly, so these new ways of expressing spirituality might sometimes overlap with traits traditionally associated with OCD—like ritualistic behaviors aimed at reducing distress or anxiety about the universe and our place in it.

Do you remember that falling sequence? That was just insane. Yeah, exactly. That whole scene was like, "We need to outdo the last one," you know? I guess that's part of the fun, though. I just wish they'd done a bit more character development. Totally. Ethan Hunt barely has time to breathe, let alone actually show us what's going on in his head. And then there's the supporting cast. Lincoln's basically the only one who gets any actual development. True. Plus, the villain barely speaks and just seems like a generic "evil genius." Almost like they were phoning it in, which I hope isn't the case with the next one. Despite all that, it's still an enjoyable watch. Even the fight scene in the train was pretty neat, but the 'Rae part was just too much. Haha, the 'Rae part. I mean, credit where credit's due for trying something different, but it was just... A bit too much, like you said. I mean, they could've shown more of that and less of the generic spy stuff. Agreed. But would that change it from being a Mission: Impossible film? Probably not. Probably not. It's hard when you've got such high expectations built up over the years, you know? For sure. The trailer promised a certain level of bananas action, and it delivered. But it could've done more with its potential. Definitely. While we're on changing expectations, any plans for the stag do this summer? I heard you were considering something out of the country? Yeah, I've been thinking about that. A week in Berlin with the lads, or maybe Prague. Haven't decided yet, to be honest. It's just so many good places! Berlin sounds like a blast. Did you meet anyone from uni who's also going out there? Yeah, a few from the course. It should be fun. Always a bit of nerves with these things, though.

So tell me everything about your weekend. I heard you've been binge-watching your favorite show; how are you doing? Well, it's been pretty quiet actually. Got some well-deserved relaxation time after that stressful week at work. I finished up the last season of Broadchurch and then started on something new because I kind of feel like I need a new emotional investment. Ah, Broadchurch, right? I’ve heard it’s phenomenal. I need to get around to watching it though; everyone says it’s so intense and intriguing. It is. You'll need to brace yourself, though. It really sucks you in. But yeah, I just had a chill weekend, nothing too eventful. Sounds nice, but what about the health side of things? How’s your recent initiative to get fit been going? Honestly, I slacked off this weekend, but I do feel like I've been consistently doing well. I’m thinking maybe I need to start jogging now that the weather is getting cooler. It was gross when it was so hot, you know. Definitely. I started a new yoga routine on Sundays, and I find it really helps to balance everything out. That sounds perfect! I’ve been interested in giving yoga a shot; it seems like the kind of thing that also helps with stress. Well, it’s super helpful for mindfulness and flexibility too. Honestly, I feel much more grounded after doing it regularly. Mindful of your breathing and all that, right? And flexibility, yeah that can't hurt. Maybe we can even practice together sometime, it'll be fun and we can catch up more regularly. I’d love that! We can schedule it during the week, or grab brunch and then yoga afterward together. Perfect. Now, speaking of foundations, how’s everything with your family? I know your mom was quite unwell earlier this year? She’s doing much better, actually. We’ve all just been keeping on top of things. She’s on her medication and is being more careful. That’s wonderful to hear. I’m sure it’s still so much to handle but it sounds like you’ve all adjusted to a new normal. We have. It’s been a bit of an adjustment, but we’re managing. We just make sure to check in regularly and if anything escalates, we now know what to do.

So tell me about your week, did you manage to finish your's plant experiment? Yeah, it's going surprisingly well. The varieties of mint I talked about before are really responding to the various light treatment. It's fascinating to see the difference. Still, now I have to deal with the statistical analysis part which questions if I will ever have time for anything else. Ah, the eternal struggle of the academic. I'm right there with you, always buried in spreadsheets. But at least for us, data is interesting, right? I'd say we're uniquely positioned to find beauty in data. However, the part I enjoy the most is seeing how plants respond. There's something almost instinctive about watching growth. I wish I had that patience. I tried following a recipe earlier - oh, the how well that went. Hence, we're about to dive into some lapsang souchong - black tea with hints of smokiness. Let's both pretend we managed our weeks well and celebrate with a good cup of tea. A good cup or a good cup. Now that's something we can universally agree on. Now, have you heard the news about the new community garden project in town? I saw it in the paper. It sounds like they’re looking for researchers to collaborate - maybe there's an opportunity for us. That's wonderful news! A nice break from the lab, I suppose. Speaking of tea, is this the new one you mentioned? I've heard it has a strong character. And a character it has! But it's surprisingly smooth doesn't it? It's a premium tea from a local supplier that I found through a friend. They have a range of artisanal blends and I thought it would be a nice change. Definitely gives a new flavor to our drinking routine. You know it's interesting how whenever we talk about our work or experiments, we somehow circle back to food or drink. Must be our way of grounding our abstract concepts in everyday life. Well, who needs therapy when you have a good cup of tea and someone to talk to? But on a more serious note, that community garden project could be a great opportunity. We might consider if it fits within the scope of our ongoing research. True. It could potentially offer new data points and perhaps new plant varieties to test.

Ah, Phil, did you manage any gardening this weekend or was it just football gods today? Yeah, I managed a bit. Had to tidy up before the predicted storms and of course, watering all the new additions in the vegetable garden. That's great! I had a bit of a mess clearing up the leaves that came down last week. Kept getting distracted by the young snooker prodigy, Jamie, of course, as he always does. Ah, keeps coming up with new tricks. Crazy kid. Yeah, but very gifted. Says he’s practicing for the next tournament, sticking by the pint-sized table he set up in his backyard. He'll be the next Ronnie O'Sullivan if he keeps that up. Probably has to be more careful than Ronnie with certain table manners, though, I'd imagine. Ron didn’t exactly set an example in that department, did he? Well, that aside, speaking of young talent, he was showing off a goal of this young player on his phone from the weekend's match. Now that kid has talent for football. I saw that goal. Was it the one with the 20-yard lob over the keeper? Yes, yes, that very one. Ah, the audacity of youth! A lob over the keeper, no less. He's got the skill level of a pro already. It’s all about timing and technique, but that kid’s instincts are on point doesn’t learn that stuff by chance. Absolutely. Reminds me of our marking, we've got all these talented students who are so much better at certain skills than I ever was at their age. Marking is a different story. The pressure on our kids to perform well is immense, and we can't help but feel responsible for helping guide them and honestly, it can be quite a task changing the world views of some of our younger students. Absolutely, but it’s rewarding when you see them grasping complex ideas. Mostly it’s rewarding when they learn to question the ideas we’ve taught them! That’s the best part about teaching, isn’t it? When they start questioning everything. Yeah, and sometimes you find yourself questioning your own knowledge after one of those conversations. For sure. Now, speaking of young talents and beginnings, did you hear about that young lad joining the police force... Oh yes, that’s big news in Tredegar.
